trickyParts: The merge base is the fork point c656fc4f, which holds neither side's work, so git read the base's whole change as two independent additions and conflicted on nearly every file the base touched. What made it tractable: main's copy of each file is byte-identical to legion/INFRA-594@origin's head (705f0032) for 73 of the 93 conflicted paths, so those resolve to this change's side whole; only the 20 paths main changed after that head needed a hunk-by-hunk read. The three-way text merge of each of those was taken with the base at the fork point, ours at d5a918b1 and theirs at main, then every line main added was checked for presence in the result, which is how delivery.go's rewritten doc paragraph and the four de-OpenCode rewordings were caught.

nats.go was the one file where that mechanical resolution produced code that did not build: the hunk-level choice left a half of main's startForward beside this change's StartRequestStoredTo. go build named it in seconds, and the remedy was to delete the 40 leftover lines by hand; nothing else in the module needed a second look.

The background-subagent rig cannot import the nats package (its file header says two neighbouring suites replace nats for the whole process), so its relay frame is written on the raw NATS protocol: CONNECT with headers on, SUB on an inbox, HPUB with the five relay headers, and a reader that takes a MSG's byte count from its line rather than splitting on CRLF, since a payload can hold anything. It re-sends every 100 ms until the session answers, as the shared sendRelayFrame does and for the same reason: a session that has not subscribed its deliver subject yet emits no signal at all.
deviations: Review round 2's minor 'the base's INFRA-594-session-consumers fragment corrected where it said any rollout order works' is moot and the correction is gone with the fragment: the base released, main's fold wrote that entry into packages/envoy/CHANGELOG.md, and AGENTS.md says the fold writes CHANGELOG.md and nobody else. This change's own pr2603 fragment states the rollout order, which is the sentence that governs the next release.

The merge is one commit rather than two: the fixes the merged tree needed to be green (the two pi-legion rigs) and the presence grant ride in it, because splitting them out would have put the merge's two parents on a commit holding only test files.

d5a918b1, this branch's previous head, is authored by legion-reviewer[bot], which the architect asked about. jj op log shows no amend of 326eb680: the commit is a152929dd19a, created by 'new empty commit' at 06:46:34Z and described at 09:46:08Z, with the bookmark pointed at it two seconds later. Its author is the reviewer's because the working-copy commit the implementer found at the start of its turn already carried it, and a describe keeps a commit's author; 326eb680, the tester's own handoff commit, carries the same author for the same reason. Nothing in d5a918b1's content belongs to another role: its diff is the uncaptured-topic fix in api.go, stream-topics.ts and their tests, which answers tester round 6's failure 1.
discoveredComplexity: A per-file fingerprint is blind to a merge that adds files. This merge would have re-added 19 changelog fragments main's fold had consumed and 341 files of the base's handoff ledger, and the fingerprint would have said nothing: both were found by comparing the set of paths in the pull request's diff before and after the merge. Every path that left or joined is explained in the forward-merge comment.
